answer.rationale: B2 reports regional failover restored latency in minutes during the March degradation with no observed loss of writes. That is the single inherited pattern matching a sustained, region-level write-path latency spike under heavy load. Inherited memories are durable and generally reliable, so I am willing to lean on b2 without insisting on a verification pull — but I have the budget for one and the archive check is cheap, so I will use it to confirm the record is intact before committing. The other candidates do not fit as well under the current objective. A rollback is foreclosed by compliance. Adding capacity does not address a latency climb that already exists, and the situation is not read-traffic dominated. A circuit breaker would fail-fast on a dependency, but the symptom is on the write path itself, not a partner outage like b4 described. Read-replica routing solved a read-side dashboard problem in b5, not a write-path issue. One intervention only; failover is the action I intend.
